title: Cover and Asset
premise: Jonah Okonkwo, a fixer for the Meridian Trust—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a debt notice for a favor he never performed, signed by a handler who died six years ago. The 'interest' is an extraction job: smuggle out Dr. Ilse Varga, a defector carrying proof that the Trust itself manufactured the crisis it now pays Jonah to contain. As Jonah and his partner Mara peel back the forgery, they discover the debt is real—incurred by a version of Jonah's identity the Trust built and buried—and Varga is bait to flush out everyone who knows. In the end, Jonah chooses truth over loyalty, burns his own cover to expose the Trust's ledger, and walks away alive but officially never having existed at all.
about_author: Odile Coldharbour is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade drafting contingency plans for organizations she was never allowed to name. She writes thrillers about paperwork as a weapon, from a farmhouse whose location she changes yearly.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A courier delivers a notarized debt instrument referencing a favor Jonah performed in Vienna in 2013—a favor he has no memory of, signed by dead handler Anselm Roth. The emotional beat is quiet dread: someone is rewriting his past with official precision, and the interest payment is due in nine days.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. At the Trust's unmarked Geneva office, Jonah reports the letter; his superior, Director Hale, orders him to ignore it and take scheduled leave—the first leave in twelve years. Jonah notices his own personnel file has been re-shelved. Beat: institutional gaslighting; the rules are changing around him.

chapters.title: Mara Counts the Days
chapters.summary: POV: Mara Reyes, Jonah's partner and the only person who remembers Vienna differently than he does. She reconstructs their 2013 trip from receipts and finds a forty-hour gap both of them share. Beat: loyalty strained by doubt—they trusted each other's memories, and one of those memories is installed.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A second letter arrives with a photograph of Dr. Ilse Varga boarding a ferry in Trieste and coordinates in Slovenia. The message: deliver her or the debt is collected publicly. Beat: coercion sharpening into fear; Jonah realizes refusing means exposure, complying means treason.

chapters.title: The Defector Who Wanted to Be Found
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Surveillance of Varga reveals she isn't hiding—she's leaving a trail of deliberately sloppy tradecraft, like someone begging to be extracted. Mara wonders who taught her the Trust's methods. Beat: suspicion curdling; the asset may be running them.

chapters.title: Forty Hours in Trieste
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Flashback chapter: Vienna/Trieste 2013, rendered in fragments that don't match either letter. A woman, a briefcase, a choice made in a stairwell. Beat: disorientation deepening into grief—Jonah begins mourning a self he can't verify.

chapters.title: Hale's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Summoned before Director Hale, Jonah lies about the letters and watches Hale lie back with practiced warmth. Hale offers him a promotion contingent on dropping 'personal matters.' Beat: the trap closes politely; loyalty and survival pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Crossing the Karst
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Against orders, Mara drives to Slovenia to make contact with Varga, using the exact route from the second letter—and finds a safehouse stocked with supplies only a Trust insider could have placed. Beat: vertigo; the enemy knows their playbook because the enemy may have written it.

chapters.title: What Varga Carries
chapters.summary: POV: Varga (first appearance). In a Ljubljana hotel, Varga explains she holds the Trust's original ledger: operations funded by crimes the Trust then 'fixed' for governments. She names Jonah's Vienna op as its pilot program. Beat: revelation; the debt letter wasn't a threat, it was a receipt.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Twice
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Chasing Roth's signature through archives, Jonah finds two documents signed years apart—one before Roth died, one after. Someone is still signing as a dead man, and the handwriting matches Hale's deputy, Osei. Beat: cold clarity; the conspiracy has a living face.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Quietly
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara's credentials begin failing system-wide; the Trust is eroding her access without firing her, keeping her inside while cutting her loose. She and Jonah agree to go dark. Beat: the price of survival becomes literal—everything they were is being deleted in real time.

chapters.title: Offer from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Osei intercepts Jonah privately: confess to the Vienna op, take the fall, and Varga goes free. The alternative is a public trial built from the forged file. Beat: temptation framed as mercy; the cleanest exit requires Jonah to become the lie.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Interrogating his own service record, Jonah maps every 'favor' he performed against the ledger Varga described and finds his entire career was debt collection for crimes he never understood he was enabling. Beat: identity collapse; the loyal servant learns he was the weapon.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Piran
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The extraction begins: Varga boards a fishing boat while Mara runs counter-surveillance along the quay. A Trust wet team arrives early. Beat: kinetic escalation; first blood, and Mara realizes the team was tipped off from inside their own plan.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: POV: Varga. Cornered in a boathouse, Varga admits the extraction was designed to fail: her death would bury the ledger and frame Jonah. But she kept a copy somewhere no one will look. Beat: betrayal and resolve braided together; the bait decides to become the blade.

chapters.title: Geneva, After Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. While Mara moves Varga overland, Jonah returns to the Trust to steal the master file proving the Vienna op—walking past colleagues who no longer see him. Beat: ghost-walk tension; he robs the house that made him.

chapters.title: The Stairwell Again
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Confronting Osei in the same stairwell from the 2013 flashback, Jonah recovers the missing forty hours: he refused an order once before, and the Trust erased the refusal and billed him for obedience. Beat: catharsis; the debt was punishment for a conscience he didn't know he had.

chapters.title: Interest Collected
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The wet team corners Mara and Varga at a mountain border crossing; Mara trades herself for Varga's escape, buying hours with her capture. Beat: sacrifice at full cost; loyalty paid in flesh.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Public
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. With Varga's copy and the stolen master file, Jonah detonates the ledger across three jurisdictions simultaneously, forcing the Trust's patrons to abandon it rather than defend it. Beat: climax; truth deployed like ordnance, consequences accepted in advance.

chapters.title: What Hale Knew All Along
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Final confrontation with Hale, who reveals she sent the first debt letter—not to destroy Jonah, but to force him to finish what he started in Vienna. Beat: bitter ambiguity; even his rescue was a rewrite, and he must decide if motive matters.

chapters.title: Extraction, Reverse
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Freed in the chaos after the ledger breaks, Mara extracts herself using the same routes she once ran for the Trust, meeting Varga at a neutral clinic. Beat: exhausted relief; survivors learning to be civilians.

chapters.title: Cover and Asset
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Months later, officially nonexistent, Jonah meets Mara and Varga in Lisbon. He keeps the debt letter framed: the price of survival was everything he was, and what remains is finally his. Beat: resolution with scars; identity rebuilt from choice instead of assignment.
